Class Terminal

Namespace
Tuinet
Assembly
Tuinet.dll

An immediate-mode terminal session: the alternate screen (or, with Tuinet.TerminalOptions.Inline, a band under the prompt), raw input, double-buffered output.

Single-threaded: call Tuinet.Terminal.Poll(Tuinet.Event@,System.Int32), Tuinet.Terminal.BeginFrame and Tuinet.Terminal.Present from one thread. Tuinet.Terminal.Post(System.Object) may be called from any thread to wake the loop. 

using var term = Terminal.Open();
while (running)
{
    if (!term.Poll(out Event ev, Timeout.Infinite)) continue;
    do { running = app.Handle(ev); } while (running && term.Poll(out ev, 0)); // coalesce bursts
    CellBuffer frame = term.BeginFrame();
    app.Render(frame);
    term.Present();                                                             // one write
}

Or implement Tuinet.IApp and let Tuinet.Terminal.Run(Tuinet.IApp,System.Int32) be that loop.

public sealed class Terminal : IDisposable

CopyToClipboard(ReadOnlySpan<char>)

Copy text to the system clipboard through the terminal (OSC 52), which also works over SSH. Returns false, sending nothing, when it is longer than Tuinet.Terminal.MaxClipboardBytes in UTF-8. Terminals may ignore it or ask the user first (it's often off by default, e.g. in tmux without set-clipboard on); there is no reply saying whether it worked.

PrintAbove(StyledText)

Inline mode: print text above the band, as ordinary terminal output that stays in the scrollback (logs over a progress bar). Long lines wrap; a trailing newline is ignored. The band moves down (the screen scrolls once it reaches the bottom) and is repainted, all in one write.

public void PrintAbove(StyledText text)

Parameters

Run(IApp, int)

Run app until its Tuinet.IApp.Handle(Tuinet.Event,System.Int64) returns false: draw a frame, sleep until input (or the next animation frame, or Tuinet.IApp.NextDueMs(System.Int64)), handle every event already waiting, draw once. A burst of key repeats costs one frame, and an idle app costs nothing. In inline mode, the last frame is drawn again after the app stops, since it stays on screen. Allocates nothing per frame; apps that need something else can keep writing their own loop with Tuinet.Terminal.Poll(Tuinet.Event@,System.Int32), Tuinet.Terminal.BeginFrame and Tuinet.Terminal.Present.

using var term = Terminal.Open();
    term.Run(new MyApp());
public void Run(IApp app, int frameMs = 33)

Parameters

app IApp

Handles events and draws frames.

frameMs int

Time between frames while Tuinet.IApp.IsAnimating(System.Int64); 0 draws as fast as the terminal takes them.

SetTitle(ReadOnlySpan<char>)

Set the window (or tab) title (OSC 2). Control characters are dropped. The terminal's own title comes back on exit where it supports the title stack (CSI 22 t / CSI 23 t). Cheap to call every frame: only a change is sent.

public void SetTitle(ReadOnlySpan<char> title)

Parameters

title ReadOnlySpan<char>

Suspend()

Leave the screen, restore the terminal and stop the process (Unix job control, as Ctrl+Z does in a shell command). Returns once the process is continued (e.g. fg), back on the alternate screen; the next Tuinet.Terminal.Poll(Tuinet.Event@,System.Int32) returns a Tuinet.EventKind.Resize event so the app draws a frame, which repaints everything. Returns false, doing nothing, where suspending isn't supported (Windows).

if (ev.Key.IsCtrl('z')) term.Suspend();

See also Tuinet.TerminalOptions.SuspendOnCtrlZ.

public bool Suspend()
